einzeiler: Why gold's recent pullback is just a pause before reaching new record highs.
kurzfassung: Gold has experienced an elongated pause after its January peak due to shifts in Fed leadership and geopolitical tensions in the Middle East. Despite these disruptions, structural drivers like heavy central bank accumulation and a debasement of fiat currency remain intact. Consequently, analysts view the current market as a buying opportunity with a solid floor near 4,000.
stichpunkte: Gold's recent pullback is classified as an elongated pause rather than the end of a bull market
Key drivers for the pause include uncertainty around the Fed chair nomination and U.S.-Iran conflict impacts
Central bank gold purchases have more than doubled since the Russia-Ukraine conflict, reducing available supply
Energy disruptions in the Middle East have constrained reserve accumulation and Asian physical demand
Silver exhibits higher volatility driven largely by retail and industrial demand compared to institutional gold
The 4,000 level is viewed as a solid structural floor supported by sovereign and institutional buying

clips.hook: Central bank accumulation is the one flow that remains
clips.text: Central bank demand continues to support the market while other large positioning sees significant reductions, pointing toward an eventual resumption of the bull trend.

clips.hook: Central banks doubled their gold purchases
clips.text: Annual central bank buying surged from roughly 400 to 500 tons up to 1,100 tons following the events in Ukraine, radically tightening the available supply funnel.

clips.hook: Silver can clear at vastly different price levels
clips.text: Retail and physical demand dynamics mean silver prices can fluctuate wildly anywhere between fifty and one hundred dollars per ounce.

clips.hook: 4,000 is a pretty solid floor for gold
clips.text: Sovereign and institutional sponsorship at this specific price point makes scaling into a long position attractive ahead of upcoming FOMC decisions.

beschreibung:
Gold set a record high in January, but uncertainty about US interest rates and disruption from the Iran war have led to an “elongated pause” in the rally, according to Tony Kim, global head of Metals Trading in Goldman Sachs FICC and Equities. Ultimately, Kim expects strong central bank demand for the yellow metal to help drive gold to new highs, he says on The Markets podcast. Kim also discusses whether fiscal sustainability concerns could spur a rotation into gold, how reduced investment demand from Asia is impacting gold markets, and why silver has been volatile in 2026.
